![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14231667/assets/e9610ceabe4a1e82995e589f482887dd9f4325218cfb5d37b5795dcb5a3bbbdc.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{9}{8},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{9}{8}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{9}{8} & =\frac{4x-2}{3x+1} \\ 9(3x+1) & =8(4x-2) \\ 27x+9 & =32x-16 \\ 9+16 & =32x-27x \\ 25 & =5x \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =4x-2=4(5)-2=18, \\ AC & =3x+1=3(5)+1=16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16\cdot 18 \\  & =144.\end{aligned}
$$
